items.title: Rudy Mazzari Interview, 1959-11-06
items.q: The interviewer asks 'Did Hill... let's see, did Heifetz ever play with you', implying 'Hill' is likely a misidentification or a different person not directly connected to the interviewee in the provided text. The interviewee responds about Heifetz, not Hill. No direct interaction or relationship be

ctx.x: So I played and then while I was playing, he said, that's enough! So I walked off and about a few minutes later, the manager of the orchestra, Mr. Frank Minor was his name, he came over and he says, well, he says, uh, uh, Dr. Svisky has decided to let you join the orchestra again, but you must try to practice, you must try to improve. He says, he thinks you're doing very badly. And funny part of ours is that everybody else said that I was doing a real singing job, playing bass, you know. So I went through, oh,…
Did Hill, uh, let's see, did Heifetz ever play with you when you were there? Oh, in, in Indianapolis? Uh-huh.

Oh, yes. And how? Heifetz played many times. I remember, he used to come every year. In fact, I remember one year, we're scheduled to do a Beethoven violin concerto. And, uh, of course, uh, Szyzki always had to rehearse the orchestra part first. Very important, you know. I remember one time, he was, every time he came to the bass passages, which are very prominent in Beethoven, he would just say, bass is too loud, bass is too loud. So he got us cut down to a whisper. Well, uh, the day when Heifetz came to…
